newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures trim losses as NY edges up.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures trim losses as NY edges up.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures recovered much of the day's losses in the afternoon, helped by small gains in New York, but the market still ended slightly down. "New York failed to go down and rallied on short-covering and London followed with it," said one trader.

Traders had expected the U.S. market to drift lower after what some called a bearish CFTC Commitment of Traders Report released on Friday. The report showed an increase in total speculative long positions.

"It was a bit bearish...it was slightly larger than I expected to be but it wasn't big enough to move the market," the trader said. "We did think it might be some sympathetic selling but it didn't happen."
By the close, benchmark January stood $3 lower at $1,422 a tonne after slipping to a session low of $1,412, just above a key support of $1,410.
But expiring November was unchanged at $1,570, thus keeping the Nov/Jan spread at a wide $148.
Traders said the November contract was seen supported by light short-covering activity ahead of its expiry this Friday.
"Spot November looks squeezed at the moment," the trader said.

New York's Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange is due to release the latest weekly exchange-certified coffee stocks and pending gradings after the close of trading on Monday. The stocks have been virtually nil and traders said the 1,250 bags of coffee pending grading by the exchange had disappeared.
"The coffee is not there any more," said one.
This week's activity is expected to stay thin due to New York's closure for Thanksgiving later this week.
"Many people have set their books for the time being. They won't want to extend themselves because of the long holiday," said one.
Technically, analysts said London's January contract remained out of danger if it held above $1,400.
On the upside, resistance is seen at $1,459 followed by the top of the current range at $1,476.
In other news, UK research firm LMC International said world consumer coffee stocks rose to 9.10 million 60-kg bags at end-September from 8.83 million in June but down from 10.94 million a year ago.

Traders said under the spotlight this week are Brazilian coffee estimates for 1997/98. A report by former USDA crop watcher Leon Yallouz could take centre stage this week as it may be the first independent forecast. --Jalil Hamid, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4985
